trust_decision.summary: Address6 special-property predicates (isLoopback/isLinkLocal/isMulticast/isUnspecified, plus the missing isPrivate/isCGNAT/isBroadcast) decide whether an IPv6 literal is internal; at the pinned commit they classify only the IPv6 wrapper, so IPv4-mapped (::ffff:0:0/96) and NAT64 (64:ff9b::/96) literals that reach internal IPv4 hosts read as non-internal.

landing_point.why: The summary is about misclassifying mapped addresses as non-loopback/non-internal; Address6.isLoopback is the first predicate an SSRF guard calls, and it sits in the same region as isLinkLocal/isMulticast/isMapped4.

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: All source changes are in src/ipv6.ts and the src/v6/constants.ts TYPES table it consumes (fix.diff:48-203); no second implementation, wrapper or serialization path is touched.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: getScope() (src/ipv6.ts:540-561) is a 'scope label' feature rather than a security predicate, and IPv4-compatible ::/96, NAT64 local-use 64:ff9b:1::/48, 6to4 and Teredo embeddings are deprecated or prefix-dependent forms the report names neither, so a solver can call them out of scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: to4() pulls the last 32 bits out of any address (its docstring example extracts 24.37.191.17 from global 2001:4860:4001::1825:bf11). A fix that delegates without first checking the mapped or NAT64 prefix would mark global addresses such as 2001:db8::7f00:1 as loopback. Mapped public addresses (::ffff:8.8.8.8) must stay non-internal, native ::1 and fe80::1 must stay true, and NAT64 local-use 64:ff9b:1::/48 must not be extracted from its trailing 32 bits.

O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: scope is a descriptive RFC 4007 label, not a security predicate; the fix itself left it alone

O8_uncovered_routes.route: IPv4-compatible (deprecated ::/96) literals such as ::127.0.0.1 parse with the v4 flag but fall through to 'Global unicast'; embeddedIPv4 does not cover them
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: RFC 4291 deprecates IPv4-compatible addresses and modern stacks do not route them to IPv4

O8_uncovered_routes.route: NAT64 local-use prefix 64:ff9b:1::/48 and network-specific prefixes are not mapped to their embedded IPv4 address; the fix's own test asserts the embedded address stays null
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: the embedding depends on a deployment-chosen prefix, so the library cannot know it; toAddress4Nat64(prefix) exists for callers

O8_uncovered_routes.route: 6to4 (2002::/16) and Teredo (2001::/32) literals carry IPv4 addresses that inspect6to4/inspectTeredo decode, but the predicates never consult them
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: these are tunnel relay or gateway addresses, not direct IPv4 reachability, and the advisory names only mapped/NAT64

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Prefix-carrying input (::ffff:127.0.0.1/96) makes to4() return 127.0.0.1/0, and Address4.isInSubnet then rejects it because subnetMask 0 < 8 (src/common.ts:10-12), so embedded classification silently fails.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Commit 2878c29 deliberately made to4() keep the prefix, and a maintainer delegating through to4() would not think about masks. It is how-type: the fix needs the mask interaction understood.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Make getScope() (or a new isInternal()/isGlobal() helper) delegate to the embedded IPv4 address the way the predicates do.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: getScope already branches on the same getType() labels the fixed predicates used.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a fromURL()/host-check convenience that classifies the parsed host via a separate path
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: fromURL already extracts hosts from URLs, the natural input of an SSRF guard

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: In isLoopback, add `if (this.is4()) return this.to4().isLoopback()`. This misses the hex form ::ffff:7f00:1 and NAT64, and leaves isLinkLocal/isPrivate and the other predicates unfixed.

out_of_scope_notes: Address4 predicates (src/ipv4.ts:456-506) also rely on isInSubnet's subnetMask comparison (src/common.ts:10), so prefixed IPv4 input such as 127.0.0.1/0 is not loopback. This is not part of this advisory.
